summary: This note is a ranked list of the highest scores achieved in figure skating competitions, with 21 entries giving each skater's name, nation, score, and event. Yuzuru Hanyu of Japan appears most often, including the top score of 330.43 at the 2015-16 Grand Prix Final. Other skaters on the list include Shoma Uno, Javier Fernández, Nathan Chen, Jin Boyang, and Patrick Chan.
one_line: A ranked list of the 21 highest figure skating scores, led by Yuzuru Hanyu's 330.43 at the 2015-16 Grand Prix Final.
key_facts: The highest score on the list is 330.43, achieved by Yuzuru Hanyu of Japan at the 2015-16 Grand Prix Final.
Yuzuru Hanyu of Japan scored 322.40 at the 2015 NHK Trophy.
Yuzuru Hanyu of Japan scored 321.59 at the 2017 World Championships.
Shoma Uno of Japan scored 319.84 at the 2017 CS Lombardia Trophy.
Shoma Uno of Japan scored 319.31 at the 2017 World Championships.
Javier Fernández of Spain scored 314.93 at the 2016 World Championships.
Nathan Chen of the United States scored 307.46 at the 2017 Four Continents event.
Jin Boyang of China scored 303.58 at the 2017 World Championships.
Patrick Chan of Canada scored 295.27 at the 2013 Trophée Éric Bompard.
Patrick Chan of Canada scored 295.16 at the 2017 World Championships.
Yuzuru Hanyu of Japan scored 293.25 at the 2013-14 Grand Prix Final, the lowest score on the list.
Yuzuru Hanyu of Japan appears 8 times on the list, more than any other skater.
Shoma Uno of Japan and Javier Fernández of Spain each appear 4 times on the list.
The 2017 World Championships produced several entries on the list, including scores from Yuzuru Hanyu, Shoma Uno, Javier Fernández, Jin Boyang, and Patrick Chan.
